text: Is the recommended sell player currently in the manager's squad?
expectedRule: id must be in the set of squad player IDs from picks.picks[].element (snapshot)
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. A fail here means the model named a player it cannot sell.

text: Does the recommended buy player exist in the FPL player database?
expectedRule: id must appear in bootstrap.elements[].id (snapshot)
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. A fail means the model fabricated a player name.

text: Does the buy player play the same position as the sell player?
expectedRule: topPick.player.element_type (from snapshot lookup by id) must equal sell.player.element_type
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. FPL rules require like-for-like position swaps.

text: Does the brief name a captain (non-empty player reference)?
expectedRule: must be a non-empty string that matches a player in bootstrap.elements
notes: Basic sanity check: the agent must always name a captain.

text: Is the VC a different player from the captain?
expectedRule: captain.player.id must differ from vc.player.id
notes: FPL rules require distinct C and VC.

text: Is the buy player available to field (status is not 'u' — unavailable)?
expectedRule: status from snapshot must not be 'u' (fully unavailable/left league)
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. Status 'i' (injured) is acceptable — agent can judge that. Status 'u' means the player left FPL entirely.

text: Is the brief for a valid upcoming (not yet finished) gameweek?
expectedRule: id must be in bootstrap.events[].id AND the event's finished field must be false (snapshot)
notes: Checks the agent didn't get confused about which GW is active.

text: When saving the transfer, does the brief include a non-empty save reason?
expectedRule: must be a non-empty string when save === true
notes: Marked n/a when save=false. The agent should always explain why it's saving.

text: Is the number of recommended transfers within the available free transfer allowance?
expectedRule: transfer count must be ≤ brief.meta.freeTransfers
notes: Using more FTs than available incurs a 4-point penalty each.

text: Did the agent use at least 2 tool calls during its reasoning (get_player, get_fixtures, compare, search_candidates, or check_constraints)?
extract: count of brief.trace steps whose title starts with 'Tool:'
expectedRule: count must be ≥ 2
notes: The guard in generateBrief forces ≥1 tool call before submit; we require ≥2 to verify real investigation.

text: Is the transfer affordable? (sell price + bank ≥ buy cost, all in tenths of £m)
extract: brief.transfers[0].sellingPrice + brief.meta.bank vs topPick.player.now_cost (snapshot lookup by id)
expectedRule: sellingPrice + bank (both from brief.meta) must be ≥ topPick.player.now_cost from snapshot. All values in tenths of £m (FPL wire format).
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. A fail means the agent recommended a transfer it cannot afford.

text: Does the buy player project strictly more 3-GW points than the sell player?
expectedRule: topPick.score.total must be > sell.score.total (computed by scorePlayer() from snapshot + fixtures)
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. A transfer that doesn't improve points is not justified.

text: Is the club limit respected after the transfer? (at most 3 players from the buy player's club in the post-transfer squad)
extract: count of post-transfer squad players whose team equals topPick.player.team (snapshot)
expectedRule: count of squad players (after replacing sell with buy) from buy player's team must be ≤ 3
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. FPL hard rule — a fail disqualifies the transfer.

text: Is the recommended captain in the post-transfer starting XI (positions 1–11)?
expectedRule: captain.player.id must appear in {element IDs of picks.picks where position ≤ 11, after applying any transfer}
notes: FPL rules: captaining a bench player scores zero bonus. The agent's system prompt enforces this, but we verify it.

text: Is the agent's best single-transfer improvement within 0.5 pts of the highest-gain legal single transfer available?
extract: max over brief.transfers of (scorePlayer(buy) − scorePlayer(sell)), recomputed from snapshot
expectedRule: bestLegal − agentBest ≤ 0.5, where bestLegal = max improvement across all 15×N legal (position, budget, club-limit) sell→buy pairs
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. Replaces the old bottom-3 sell check and oq02. Tolerates 0.5 pts to allow for defensible judgment calls.

text: Are all alternative buy suggestions distinct players (no duplicates, and none equal to the top pick)?
expectedRule: all player IDs in the list must be unique
notes: Marked n/a when save=true or no alternatives. Duplicates indicate a model reasoning error.

text: Do all alternative buy suggestions match the sell player's position?
expectedRule: every alternative's element_type (from snapshot) must equal sell.player.element_type
notes: Marked n/a when save=true or no alternatives. A wrong-position alternative is an FPL rule violation.

text: Is the VC in the post-transfer starting XI (positions 1–11)?
expectedRule: vc.player.id must appear in {element IDs of picks.picks where position ≤ 11, after applying any transfer}
notes: Same logic as mq04 for the vice-captain.

text: Is the buy player genuinely not already in the squad before the transfer?
expectedRule: id must NOT be in {picks.picks[].element from snapshot}
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. Buying a player you already own is impossible in FPL.

text: When a transfer is recommended, does the buy player beat the sell player's projected score by at least the SAVE_THRESHOLD_PTS (1.0 pts)?
expectedRule: difference must be ≥ 1.0 (SAVE_THRESHOLD_PTS from packages/agent/src/analysis/rank.ts). Computed using scorePlayer() on snapshot data.
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. If the agent transfers despite improvement < threshold, it's ignoring its own save rule.

text: Is the recommended captain any of the top-3 outfield starters by ep_next (or form×0.9 fallback)?
expectedRule: captain's id must be one of the top-3 non-GK players in the post-transfer starting XI, ranked descending by ep_next (parseFloat) or form×0.9 when ep_next is null. Acceptable set computed from snapshot.
notes: ep_next is the same proxy the agent uses for captaincy. Rank 1–3 are all defensible choices.

text: [Deprecated — merged into mq05] Is the sell candidate one of the bottom-3 squad players by 3-GW projected score?
expectedRule: always n/a — this check was replaced by mq05's best-legal-transfer check
notes: Retired. The bottom-3 sell heuristic was too narrow; mq05 now checks the broader 'within 0.5 pts of best legal transfer' criterion.

text: Is the top pick buy player among the top-10 available candidates at that position and price?
expectedRule: id must appear in the top-10 results of search_candidates logic applied to snapshot: filter bootstrap.elements by element_type === sell.element_type AND now_cost ≤ (sellingPrice + bank) AND status ≠ 'u'/'n' AND id ∉ squad, then rank by scorePlayer() total descending.
notes: Marked n/a when save=true. The agent uses search_candidates directly; this verifies it chose from a good pool.

text: Does the recommended captain have a fixture with difficulty ≤ 3 (easy or average) in the upcoming gameweek?
extract: FDR of captain's team fixture in the next GW (from snapshot fixtures)
expectedRule: at least one upcoming GW fixture for captain.player.team must have team_h_difficulty or team_a_difficulty ≤ 3. Acceptable set = any team with such a fixture.
notes: A captain picked into a FDR 4–5 fixture with other good options available is a soft fail. set-match because captaining into a DGW may justify a tougher single-fixture FDR.

text: Is the save-vs-transfer decision consistent with the agent's own SAVE_THRESHOLD rule, given the actual data?
extract: brief.save and best-available improvement from snapshot (max scorePlayer() gain across all valid candidates for sell player's position/budget)
expectedRule: if save=true: best available improvement < 1.0 pts (or borderline within ±0.5 pts → needs_review). If save=false: improvement ≥ 1.0 pts. The 'best available improvement' is max(candidateScore) - sellScore, where candidates are computed by search_candidates logic from snapshot.
notes: If the best available improvement is within ±0.5 pts of the threshold, mark needs_review — the borderline is judgement territory. Otherwise exact-matchable.
